key_insight: A compact CMOS+X neuron that pairs a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) in series with an NMOS transistor can produce biologically realistic, nonlinear spiking dynamics, enabling expressive nonlinear classification without adding complex circuitry.
problem_solved: How to realize nonlinear, expressive computation in spiking neurons using compact, energy-efficient hardware (CMOS+X) without relying on extra circuit complexity or large area/power overhead.
method: Design a CMOS+X spiking neuron by connecting an MTJ in series with an NMOS transistor to produce intrinsic nonlinear voltage/current dynamics.

Use circuit-level simulations to characterize the neuron’s dynamical regimes (spiking thresholds, adaptation, bifurcations) and show how those dynamics implement nonlinear input–output transformations useful for classification.
Demonstrate the neuron’s classification-relevant behavior via simple nonlinear decision tasks and compare functional trade-offs relevant to area, energy, and circuit simplicity.
impact: Provides a hardware-native mechanism for nonlinear computation in spiking networks, enabling more expressive, energy-efficient on-device AI and simplifying neuromorphic chip design by reducing extra circuit blocks.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of the CMOS+X neuron (MTJ in series with NMOS) with labeled terminals and current flow.
Phase portrait / I–V curve showing nonlinear regimes and spiking threshold behavior.
Spike-timing rasters or membrane-equivalent waveform illustrating classification-triggered responses to different input patterns.
Mini bar chart or infographic comparing area/energy/complexity trade-offs vs. conventional approaches (qualitative).
paper_title: Biologically Realistic Dynamics for Nonlinear Classification in CMOS+X Neurons
paper_authors: Steven Louis, Hannah Bradley, Artem Litvinenko, Cody Trevillian, Darrin Hanna
